EXPLOIT BOOTSTRAPPING
OPPORTUNITIES
Bootstrapping = Resourcing your needs without being dependent on external finance over the long
term
Examples:
− Short-term borrowing or lending tools, machinery etc., to other businesses
− Co-ordinate buying supplies with other businesses
− Receiving a loan from family, relatives or friends
EXPLOIT BOOTSTRAPPING OPPORTUNITIES
More bootstrapping methods:
− Negotiating late payments from the subcontractor
• Receive advance payments from customers
− Apply interest to late payments from customers.
− Sharing the company's land and buildings with other
businesses
− Share employees with other businesses
− Share tools with other companies
▪ Utilise resources when they aren’t normally in use

CASE STUDY:
Sophie and The Delivery Service
Sophie has a small restaurant where she sells snacks and some dishes. The restaurant is located in a
very friendly corner near a main street in the city centre. In the beginning she didn’t make much profit
from her restaurant. However, she was successful because she was persistent in developing her
business. In addition, she received financial support from her brother and also sought credit from a
local bank.
In recent months, some customers have complained that they have to walk a long way to the
restaurant at midday in the sun. Sophie therefore had the idea of investing in a delivery service. She
has set herself the following target for the end of the year:
"Delivering two different dishes during the lunch hour to customers in the surrounding areas
Now Sophie needs to know
-How she can reach her goal
-What resources are needed to achieve it

Exercise: Financial sources for your goal
Instruction:
Working in the same groups as before.
1. Note down your existing financial sources for achieving your goals. Discuss and note the advantages
and disadvantages of each of these sources.
2. Next, make a list of unusual financial sources - think of ALL the possible ways to get or save money that
others may not think of. Discuss and note the advantages and disadvantages of these sources.
Ask yourself:
• Are these sources really new and not just a copy of what others are already doing?
• Do you think these sources will work in the future?
• Do these sources really help me to overcome the financial challenges of my business?
